en.statement: The AWS Well-Architected Framework puts cost optimization ahead of reliability in pillar tradeoffs.
en.explanation: Pillar tradeoffs depend on business needs; a mission-critical workload can justify higher costs to improve reliability.

en.statement: Amazon Neptune suits applications that query relationships in highly connected data.
en.explanation: Amazon Neptune is a managed graph database. Its graph model supports relationship-heavy use cases such as fraud detection and recommendation engines.

en.statement: AWS Organizations can share eligible Amazon EC2 Reserved Instance discounts across member accounts.
en.explanation: Consolidated billing supports sharing eligible Reserved Instance discounts across accounts in AWS Organizations. Discount sharing lets another account benefit from unused discounts.

en.statement: AWS connects Availability Zones within a Region through the public internet.
en.explanation: AWS interconnects Availability Zones with redundant, dedicated network links. These links support high-bandwidth, low-latency communication within a Region.

en.statement: Repurchasing replaces an existing application with another product, such as a SaaS offering.
en.explanation: Repurchasing switches products instead of moving the existing application, for example by adopting a vendor-hosted software service.

en.statement: AWS Knowledge Center provides personalized status updates for a customer's open support cases.
en.explanation: AWS Knowledge Center provides answers to common troubleshooting questions. It is a self-service knowledge resource, rather than a system for tracking private support cases.

en.statement: AWS Direct Connect carries its connection to AWS over the public internet.
en.explanation: AWS Direct Connect provides a private network path to AWS that bypasses the public internet. It connects your network through a Direct Connect location.

en.statement: Amazon EC2 On-Demand pricing is a good fit for short-term workloads with unpredictable compute needs.
en.explanation: Amazon EC2 On-Demand Instances let you pay for compute as you use it, without a long-term commitment. This suits short-lived or irregular workloads.

source.title: Purchasing On-Demand Instances for Amazon EC2

en.statement: Customers patch the operating systems that run the Amazon DynamoDB service.
en.explanation: AWS operates and maintains the infrastructure and operating systems behind Amazon DynamoDB. Customers remain responsible for their data.

en.statement: AWS CodeBuild coordinates the stages of a continuous delivery pipeline.
en.explanation: AWS CodePipeline coordinates a delivery workflow. AWS CodeBuild handles build tasks such as compiling source code and running tests within that workflow.

en.statement: Amazon DynamoDB TTL makes an expired item immediately unavailable to application read requests.
en.explanation: DynamoDB TTL deletes expired items asynchronously. Items awaiting background deletion can remain readable, so applications needing immediate expiry must check expiration themselves.

source.title: Using time to live (TTL) in DynamoDB

en.statement: A service control policy attached to the organization root restricts IAM users in the management account.
en.explanation: Service control policies do not restrict principals in the AWS Organizations management account, even when the policy is attached to the organization root.

en.statement: A VPC-connected AWS Lambda function can reach the IPv4 internet directly from a public subnet.
en.explanation: Placing a Lambda function in a public subnet does not give it internet access. IPv4 connectivity needs a suitable egress path, such as a private-subnet route through a NAT gateway.

source.title: Enable internet access for VPC-connected Lambda functions

en.statement: Amazon EventBridge event-bus rules can select events using fields nested inside the event's detail object.
en.explanation: An EventBridge event pattern can match values within detail, letting a rule select events based on their contents before forwarding them to its targets.

en.statement: Selecting a lower Amazon CloudFront price class blocks viewers located outside its included geographies.
en.explanation: CloudFront price classes select the edge locations used to serve content, not the countries allowed to view it. Viewers outside the selected locations can still receive the content.

en.statement: An AWS Site-to-Site VPN connection provides redundant tunnels to the same customer gateway device.
en.explanation: The VPN tunnels terminate at separate AWS endpoints. Configuring both on the customer gateway preserves a usable path when a tunnel is unavailable.

source.title: Tunnel options for your AWS Site-to-Site VPN connection

en.statement: A direct write to Amazon DynamoDB can leave an item cached in DynamoDB Accelerator stale.
en.explanation: A write that bypasses DAX does not refresh its item cache. Cached data can remain stale until the entry expires, is evicted, or is updated through DAX.

en.statement: Amazon DynamoDB on-demand bills throughput according to actual read and write requests.
en.explanation: On-demand capacity charges follow the requests processed rather than a provisioned throughput allocation. Idle read and write capacity adds no throughput charge.

en.statement: An Application Load Balancer can pass a client's encrypted TLS session through to targets for decryption.
en.explanation: An Application Load Balancer terminates client TLS on its HTTPS listener. HTTPS connections to targets are separate connections rather than the original client TLS session.

source.title: Listeners for your Application Load Balancers

en.statement: Amazon RDS for SQL Server offers deployments with the SQL Server software license bundled into the service price.
en.explanation: The RDS for SQL Server License Included model incorporates the SQL Server software license into RDS pricing. A separate SQL Server license purchase is unnecessary for that model.

source.title: Licensing Microsoft SQL Server on Amazon RDS

en.statement: Amazon API Gateway applies a REST API canary's stageVariableOverrides to production-release requests.
en.explanation: Canary overrides change the stage variable values used for canary requests. Production-release requests keep the stage's production values.

en.statement: AWS Lambda extracts a layer's archive into /opt in the function's execution environment.
en.explanation: Layer contents land under /opt. Package dependencies in the directory layout expected by the function's runtime so it can find them.

en.statement: CloudWatch schedules recurring SNS notifications for an alarm that remains in the ALARM state.
en.explanation: CloudWatch invokes the SNS action when the alarm changes into its configured state. Remaining in ALARM does not schedule repeated SNS notifications.

en.statement: AWS Lambda freezes a published version's environment variables at the values present during publication.
en.explanation: PublishVersion captures environment settings with the function version. Change $LATEST and publish a new version to use different values.

en.statement: Amazon ECS counts later health-check failures after a successful check during startPeriod.
en.explanation: A successful check during startPeriod marks the container healthy. Subsequent failures count toward retries even if the configured start period is still running.

source.title: Determine Amazon ECS task health using container health checks

en.statement: A Lambda function's resource-based policy grants its handler permission to call DynamoDB PutItem.
en.explanation: A Lambda function receives DynamoDB permissions through its execution role. Its resource-based policy grants other principals access to the function.

en.statement: Amazon API Gateway REST API request validation supports checking header values against a JSON schema.
en.explanation: REST API request validation checks required headers for presence and nonblank values. JSON schema validation applies to the request body.

source.title: Request validation for REST APIs in API Gateway

en.statement: DynamoDB supports strongly consistent Query requests against global secondary indexes.
en.explanation: DynamoDB global secondary indexes provide eventually consistent reads. A Query requesting strong consistency on a GSI is rejected.

en.statement: CloudWatch treats one metric name published with two different dimension values as two distinct metrics.
en.explanation: Namespace, metric name and dimensions together identify a CloudWatch metric, and statistics come back only for the dimension combinations that were published.

en.statement: Amazon DynamoDB UpdateItem applies numeric ADD updates atomically under concurrent writes.
en.explanation: Use an ADD update expression to increment the stored counter value inside DynamoDB. Concurrent increments avoid a client-side read-modify-write race.

source.title: Use atomic counter operations in DynamoDB with an AWS SDK

en.statement: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Memory extracts user preferences from earlier conversations for later interactions.
en.explanation: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Memory stores useful insights from past interactions in long-term memory. Agents use those insights to personalize later conversations.

source.title: Add memory to your Amazon Bedrock AgentCore agent

en.statement: Unsupervised learning discovers which products customers tend to purchase together.
en.explanation: Association analysis finds co-occurrence patterns in purchase records, such as items that frequently appear in the same basket.

en.statement: Prompt caching in Amazon Bedrock reuses completed answers when users repeat a question.
en.explanation: Amazon Bedrock prompt caching reuses shared input context. Reusing that context reduces the model's repeated input processing on later requests.

en.statement: Public access to a model's weights allows a business to use the model commercially.
en.explanation: A model's license governs permitted use. Public availability does not establish commercial permission; users need to check the provider's applicable terms for their use case.

en.statement: Model distillation transfers a teacher model's learned weights directly to a smaller student model.
en.explanation: A student learns from response examples produced by a teacher. Distillation passes behavioral knowledge through training data rather than copying the teacher's weights.

source.title: Customize a model with distillation in Amazon Bedrock

en.statement: Amazon Bedrock Guardrails can check both user text and model responses for harmful content.
en.explanation: Content filters examine input prompts and model responses for harmful content such as hate or violence. Filtering strength is configurable for the application's needs.

en.statement: SageMaker Model Registry tracks the approval status of model versions considered for production.
en.explanation: SageMaker Model Registry records model versions and their approval status, helping teams control which versions advance toward deployment.

source.title: Model Registration Deployment with Model Registry

en.statement: Image input support implies that a foundation model supports image generation in its responses.
en.explanation: A foundation model's accepted inputs and generated outputs are separate capabilities. A model that accepts images may return text rather than generated pictures.

en.statement: Deep neural networks need far more training examples than traditional machine learning methods.
en.explanation: Deep networks have many layers and weights to learn, so they need millions of training examples rather than the hundreds or thousands a simpler network might need.

en.statement: A foundation model keeps generated creative writing unique to the customer who requests it.
en.explanation: A foundation model's creative output may overlap with output it independently produces for another customer. Requesting original prose does not establish exclusive wording.

en.statement: AWS Shield Advanced requires a protected resource's Amazon Route 53 health check for proactive engagement.
en.explanation: AWS Shield Advanced proactive engagement uses resource health to decide whether a detected attack warrants contact from the Shield Response Team.

source.title: Setting up proactive engagement for the SRT to contact you directly

en.statement: The Rolling policy in AWS Elastic Beanstalk Standard preserves full serving capacity during an application deployment.
en.explanation: The Rolling policy takes the current batch out of service, reducing serving capacity during deployment. An architect accounts for this reduction when the workload has a capacity requirement.

en.statement: A shared EC2 cluster placement group can improve node-to-node latency for applications spanning AWS accounts.
en.explanation: AWS RAM shares a cluster placement group with other accounts. Participants place interdependent instances in the shared group and connect their VPCs to gain its latency benefits.

en.statement: When Elastic Load Balancing reports every instance unhealthy, Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling can throttle their replacement.
en.explanation: If ELB health checks report all instances unhealthy while the load balancer is InService, Auto Scaling might mark fewer of them unhealthy at a time, leaving time to fix the fault before the whole group is replaced.

source.title: About the health checks for your Auto Scaling group

en.statement: Reachability Analyzer can model a cross-account VPC path to locate network configuration blocking traffic.
en.explanation: Reachability Analyzer models routes and network controls instead of sending packets. It can analyze connected VPCs across accounts in one Region within an organization.

en.statement: An Amazon ElastiCache global datastore can automatically promote a secondary Region after a primary Region failure.
en.explanation: ElastiCache promotes a secondary global datastore cluster after an explicit cross-Region failover request. A primary Region failure by itself does not trigger this promotion.

en.statement: AWS Global Accelerator can improve a global UDP application's network path while keeping its existing regional hosts.
en.explanation: Global Accelerator carries application traffic from nearby edge locations over the AWS network to regional endpoints. Existing EC2 instances or load balancers remain the application hosts.

en.statement: Amazon ECS Anywhere can register on-premises service tasks with Elastic Load Balancing through ECS service integration.
en.explanation: ECS Anywhere excludes ECS service load balancing for external instances. A migrated on-premises web service needs a separate approach for distributing inbound traffic.

source.title: Amazon ECS clusters for external instances

en.statement: Updating a Service Quotas request template requests its new quota values for existing accounts in the organization.
en.explanation: A quota request template requests its values for accounts created in the organization after association. Updating it leaves existing accounts' quotas unchanged, so they need their own increase requests.

en.statement: After retries fail, AWS Step Functions sends matching task errors to a compensation branch configured in a catcher.
en.explanation: A catcher routes matching task errors to a fallback state defined by the architect. That path can perform compensation, such as releasing inventory reserved earlier.

source.title: Handling errors in Step Functions workflows

en.statement: AWS CloudFormation can accept a new stack update while the stack is in UPDATE_ROLLBACK_FAILED.
en.explanation: A stack in UPDATE_ROLLBACK_FAILED needs recovery before another update. The operator can use ContinueUpdateRollback to restore it to UPDATE_ROLLBACK_COMPLETE.

en.statement: Amazon RDS automatically repoints a Multi-AZ DB instance's existing DNS record to its standby during failover.
en.explanation: RDS changes the destination returned by the DB instance's DNS name during failover. Clients re-establish connections to resolve the updated destination.

source.title: Failing over a Multi-AZ DB instance for Amazon RDS

en.statement: With delivery permissions configured, CloudFront standard logging (v2) can send logs to a CloudWatch Logs log group.
en.explanation: CloudFront standard logging (v2) uses CloudWatch vended logs for delivery. Set a CloudWatch Logs log group's ARN as the destination.

en.statement: An active VPC peering connection supports routing onward through its peer's other peering connections.
en.explanation: VPC peering carries traffic between directly paired VPCs. A peer VPC does not provide transit onward through another peering connection.

en.statement: With its zone of trust set to the account, IAM Access Analyzer trusts other accounts in the same organization.
en.explanation: An external access analyzer scoped to an account trusts that account's principals. Principals in another organization member account remain outside its zone of trust.

en.statement: In AWS Organizations, an enabled AWS Control Tower detective control evaluates unenrolled accounts in its OU.
en.explanation: Control Tower detective controls apply to enrolled accounts in a registered OU. Accounts in that OU that remain unenrolled fall outside those controls.

en.statement: AWS Trusted Advisor's Security Groups – Specific Ports Unrestricted check evaluates only IPv4 inbound rules.
en.explanation: This Trusted Advisor check evaluates IPv4 ingress rules. Operators review IPv6 ingress separately rather than treating its result as an IPv6 exposure assessment.

source.title: Security checks: Security Groups – Specific Ports Unrestricted

en.statement: A CloudWatch dashboard displays metrics from different AWS Regions together in the same operational view.
en.explanation: CloudWatch dashboards bring metrics from different Regions into one view. Widget or metric settings identify the Region supplying the data.

en.statement: AWS Global Accelerator releases an accelerator's assigned static IP addresses when an operator disables the accelerator.
en.explanation: Assigned IP addresses remain with an accelerator while it exists, including while disabled. Deleting the accelerator releases its assigned addresses.

en.statement: With ALLOW_AS_DEPENDENCY, Patch Manager reports rejected Linux packages installed as dependencies as INSTALLED_OTHER.
en.explanation: Patch Manager treats a rejected Linux package installed as a dependency as compliant with the baseline and records its status as INSTALLED_OTHER.

en.statement: Amazon S3 rejects a root user's DeleteObject request naming a version ID with active compliance retention.
en.explanation: Compliance-mode S3 Object Lock protects an individual object version against deletion requests even from the account root user until its retention expires.

en.statement: Amazon EBS lets a responder preserve disk evidence at request time while snapshot transfer continues.
en.explanation: EBS snapshots preserve volume data as it exists when requested. Writes made while the snapshot transfers to Amazon S3 leave that captured disk evidence unchanged.

en.statement: AWS Organizations can register a StackSets delegated administrator with deployment privileges restricted to one OU.
en.explanation: A delegated administrator for service-managed StackSets has deployment authority across the organization. The management account cannot restrict that registration to specific OUs.

source.title: Create CloudFormation StackSets with service-managed permissions

en.statement: AWS Private CA can issue an end-entity certificate whose validity period extends past its issuing CA's expiry.
en.explanation: AWS Private CA keeps each certificate's validity within its issuing CA's, so end-entity and child CA certificates expire no later than their parent. Plan CA lifetimes back from the leaf.

en.statement: CreateResolverQueryLogConfig automatically selects the Region's existing VPCs for DNS query logging.
en.explanation: CreateResolverQueryLogConfig sets the destination. AssociateResolverQueryLogConfig selects a VPC for query-log collection.

en.statement: An IAM user's cross-account AssumeRole requires an identity policy Allow and the target role's trust policy Allow.
en.explanation: Cross-account role assumption needs the caller's identity permissions and trust from the destination role. Authorization from one account alone is insufficient.

source.title: Grant a user permissions to switch roles

en.statement: An EC2 Instance Connect SSH session stays open after the IAM credentials behind its key push expire.
en.explanation: IAM is checked when the SSH public key is pushed, not for the session's lifetime. The connection persists until the SSH session ends, so close it or set an SSH timeout on your client.

source.title: Connect to a Linux instance using EC2 Instance Connect

en.statement: AWS Security Hub CSPM cross-Region aggregation automatically enables the service in linked Regions.
en.explanation: Cross-Region aggregation collects data from Regions where Security Hub CSPM is enabled. The aggregation configuration does not enable the service there.

source.title: Understanding cross-Region aggregation in Security Hub CSPM

en.statement: AWS FIS selects tagged experiment targets when an engineer creates the experiment template.
en.explanation: AWS FIS resolves targets when the experiment starts. Tag changes between template creation and execution can therefore change the resources selected.

en.statement: AWS IoT Core thing policy variables use the MQTT client ID as the thing name under non-exclusive association.
en.explanation: With non-exclusive thing association, AWS IoT Core uses the MQTT client ID to identify the thing for policy-variable evaluation. The client ID must match that thing's registered name.

en.statement: BigQuery Omni is an operational database service for recording customer orders across multiple clouds.
en.explanation: BigQuery Omni provides analytics over data in multiple cloud environments. Its role is analytical querying rather than serving as an application's transactional order database.

en.statement: Cloud Billing reports show which Google Cloud services contribute most to an organization's costs.
en.explanation: Cloud Billing reports break down incurred costs by dimensions such as service. This helps a team identify the services driving its cloud spending.

source.title: Analyze billing data and cost trends with Reports

en.statement: Selecting tools to carry out a multistep task is a capability of agentic AI systems.
en.explanation: An agentic system can turn a goal into actions and use tools to carry them out. This extends its role beyond producing a response for a person to act on.

en.statement: Developing a model in BigQuery ML means writing Python code.
en.explanation: BigQuery ML creates and runs models from GoogleSQL queries or the Google Cloud console. Analysts build models with SQL skills they already have, without programming in Python or Java.

en.statement: BigQuery users provision database servers before running their analytical queries.
en.explanation: BigQuery provides a serverless analytical service. Google manages the underlying infrastructure rather than requiring users to provision database servers.

en.statement: An API product in Apigee packages selected API capabilities with a service plan as a business offering.
en.explanation: Apigee API products package chosen functionality into offerings for particular audiences or service tiers. This gives a business a defined unit to offer as a product.

en.statement: Data integrity protects confidential information from being viewed by unauthorized readers.
en.explanation: Data integrity concerns the accuracy and trustworthiness of information. Confidentiality concerns keeping that information from unauthorized readers.

en.statement: Dataflow runs batch and streaming data pipelines using the same programming model.
en.explanation: Dataflow uses the Apache Beam programming model across both processing modes. Teams can use a common approach to define their data-processing logic.

en.statement: Model Armor screens an AI assistant's prompts and responses for malicious instructions.
en.explanation: Model Armor evaluates prompts and model responses for threats such as prompt injection. This helps protect AI applications from attempts to manipulate their behavior.

en.statement: Cloud Profiler shows developers which application code consumes excessive CPU or memory resources.
en.explanation: Cloud Profiler attributes CPU and memory use to application code. Developers can use that information to focus optimization work on resource-intensive parts of the application.

en.statement: A standalone Google Cloud organization requires a Cloud Identity account for its creation.
en.explanation: Google Cloud creates a standalone organization for an eligible signup using a Google email address, with no Cloud Identity account required.

en.statement: VPC firewall rules logging records each packet in an allowed TCP connection.
en.explanation: VPC firewall rules logging records an allowed TCP connection once, rather than recording every packet in that connection.

en.statement: Data Access audit logs are enabled by default for Cloud Storage.
en.explanation: Data Access audit logs for Cloud Storage need explicit enablement. BigQuery is the default-enabled exception.

en.statement: A Cloud Billing budget alert can trigger from forecasted spend.
en.explanation: Cloud Billing budget threshold rules can evaluate either actual spend or forecasted spend.

source.title: Create, edit, or delete budgets and budget alerts

en.statement: With OS Login enabled, Compute Engine accepts SSH keys stored in VM metadata.
en.explanation: With OS Login enabled, Compute Engine uses keys associated with the user's Google identity and stops accepting SSH keys from project or instance metadata.

en.statement: Cloud Billing budgets accept project and service filters for cost alerts.
en.explanation: An alerts-only budget can narrow the costs it monitors to selected projects and services.

source.title: Create, edit, or delete budgets and budget alerts

en.statement: A VPC firewall rule selects the target VM instances by matching their attached secure tag values.
en.explanation: VPC firewall rules use network tags to select VMs. Secure tags select sources or targets in Cloud NGFW firewall policies.

en.statement: Cloud Router exchanges BGP routes over an HA VPN tunnel.
en.explanation: Cloud Router establishes BGP sessions over HA VPN tunnels to exchange dynamic routes with a peer network.

en.statement: Rewriting a Nearline object to Coldline within 30 days can incur an early deletion charge.
en.explanation: A storage class change by rewrite replaces the object, so Nearline's 30-day minimum storage duration is billed. Class changes by Object Lifecycle Management or Autoclass are exempt.

en.statement: The Ops Agent merges its config.yaml settings with its built-in configuration when it restarts.
en.explanation: User settings in config.yaml are merged with the built-in configuration on restart; to override a built-in receiver, processor or pipeline, redefine it with the same identifier.

en.statement: Google recommends first-mover workloads with few dependencies for teams new to Google Cloud migrations.
en.explanation: Google's first-mover guidance favors few dependencies so teams learn migration patterns before coordinating complex workload groups.

source.title: Migrate to Google Cloud: Assess and discover your workloads

en.statement: DORA groups failed deployment recovery time with deployment frequency as a software delivery throughput factor.
en.explanation: DORA measures throughput with change lead time, deployment frequency and failed deployment recovery time; change fail rate and deployment rework rate measure instability.

en.statement: The Well-Architected Framework says sole-tenant node costs can qualify as capital expenditure.
en.explanation: The cost pillar lists Compute Engine sole-tenant nodes as a service whose costs might receive capital-expenditure treatment.

en.statement: Compute Engine bases machine type recommendations on peak CPU utilization rather than sampled averages.
en.explanation: Compute Engine uses averaged CPU metrics for machine type recommendations. Short bursts can be missed, so a recommended smaller VM may lack needed burst capacity.

source.title: Apply machine type recommendations to VM instances

en.statement: Access Transparency lets a customer approve Google personnel access before engineers read customer data.
en.explanation: Access Transparency records Google personnel's actions when they access customer data. Access Approval provides the customer authorization step for covered access requests.

en.statement: Google lists an on-call intervention, such as a release rollback, among the triggers for a postmortem.
en.explanation: Google's postmortem criteria include on-call interventions such as a release rollback or rerouted traffic, alongside user-visible downtime, data loss of any kind and monitoring failures.

en.statement: Cloud Billing's detailed usage cost export can directly attribute Compute Engine charges to individual VM resources.
en.explanation: The detailed Cloud Billing export adds resource-level cost data. Teams use the VM identity in eligible usage records to investigate which instance drives spending.

source.title: Export Cloud Billing data to BigQuery

en.statement: Local SSD automatically replicates workload data to preserve it after an unrecoverable host failure.
en.explanation: Local SSD is attached to the VM's physical host and lacks automatic replication. Host errors can lose its data, so durable recovery needs another copy.

en.statement: Google recommends isolating a Spanner load test from other services when validating production peak capacity.
en.explanation: Google's Spanner launch checklist includes interacting services and realistic user journeys in load tests. Isolated database tests miss competing application and background workloads.

en.statement: Cloud Shell's VM automatically joins the selected project's VPC network for private resource access.
en.explanation: Google hosts the Cloud Shell VM outside the customer's VPC network. Selecting a project leaves that network boundary in place, so private IP access needs a separate connectivity path.

en.statement: BigQuery sharing egress restrictions let a publisher block subscribers from copying or exporting linked dataset tables.
en.explanation: With data egress restricted on a listing, copy, clone, export and snapshot operations are unavailable, and so are writes to destination tables. Publishers can also restrict query results.

en.statement: BigQuery shares idle slots between reservations in different administration projects of one organization.
en.explanation: Idle slot capacity stays within one administration project and one region. Reservations in separate administration projects, or in separate organizations, do not share idle slots.

en.statement: BigQuery bills time travel and fail-safe bytes separately when a dataset uses physical storage billing.
en.explanation: Physical storage billing charges time travel and fail-safe storage at the active storage rate. Retained historical versions therefore contribute to the dataset's storage bill.

en.statement: BigQuery ML requires reserved capacity for imported TensorFlow inference on images in object tables.
en.explanation: Running an imported TensorFlow model against image object tables uses capacity-based pricing through reservations. BigQuery excludes on-demand pricing for this inference path.

source.title: Run inference on image object tables

en.statement: Datastream writes Cloud Storage change events in the order in which the source commits them.
en.explanation: Datastream does not guarantee event delivery order to Cloud Storage. Downstream consumers use source-specific event metadata to reconstruct the source's sequence of changes.

en.statement: BigQuery ML can automatically reload an imported TensorFlow model when its files in Cloud Storage change.
en.explanation: BigQuery ML freezes an imported TensorFlow model when it creates the model. Later edits to its Cloud Storage source files leave that imported model unchanged.

source.title: The CREATE MODEL statement for importing TensorFlow models

en.statement: Dataform unit tests build their dependency tables by executing upstream workflow actions.
en.explanation: Dataform unit tests replace an action's dependencies with mock inputs, then compare its SQL result against an expected result set.

en.statement: BigQuery adds a job's labels to billing data, so a Cloud Billing export can group on-demand query charges by job label.
en.explanation: Job labels reach billing data. Dataset labels appear only in storage billing data and table or view labels not at all, so teams label jobs to attribute query costs by team or workload.

en.statement: BigQuery ML automatically standardizes numeric features during boosted tree model training.
en.explanation: BigQuery ML leaves numeric features unstandardized in its automatic preprocessing for boosted tree models. Tree models are exceptions to the numeric standardization used for many other model types.

en.statement: Dataflow supports graph-changing replacement updates for a running batch pipeline.
en.explanation: Dataflow's pipeline update feature applies to running streaming jobs. Engineers run changed batch pipeline code as another job.

en.statement: Firestore Standard edition server transactions support reading a document after queuing a write.
en.explanation: Firestore transaction code reads documents before queuing writes. Move dependent reads ahead of the transaction's set, update, or delete operations.

en.statement: Cloud Workstations' persistent home disk replaces files a custom image added under /home at build time.
en.explanation: By default a persistent disk attaches over /home when the container starts, overwriting build-time changes there. Install tools outside /home or modify /home at runtime.

en.statement: Cloud Functions v2 API supports updating functions created through the Cloud Run Admin API.
en.explanation: A function created through the Cloud Run Admin API uses that API for management. The Cloud Functions API cannot modify these Admin API-created functions.

en.statement: A Pub/Sub pull subscriber with exactly-once delivery can reuse the first acknowledgment ID after redelivery.
en.explanation: A valid redelivery creates a new acknowledgment ID. Pub/Sub accepts the latest ID; an older delivery's ID fails.

en.statement: ADC checks an environment-specified credential file before its local credential file.
en.explanation: Application Default Credentials checks the environment-specified file first, then the local ADC file, then the attached service account.

en.statement: Cloud Storage object listings include newly created objects after a successful create response.
en.explanation: Cloud Storage object listing is strongly consistent. A list request after a successful object creation reflects the newly created object.

en.statement: Eventarc Standard can guarantee source order when delivering related application events.
en.explanation: Eventarc Standard provides no delivery-order guarantee. An application that depends on sequence needs to handle events that arrive out of order.

en.statement: Cloud Run services handle bidirectional gRPC streams over HTTP/2.
en.explanation: A Cloud Run service handles streaming gRPC interfaces when the service uses HTTP/2. Bidirectional streaming is a supported gRPC interaction.

en.statement: Cloud Build's allowExitCodes takes precedence over allowFailure in a test step that sets both.
en.explanation: With allowFailure true and allowExitCodes [1], a test step that exits with 2 still fails the build, because only the listed exit codes are tolerated.

en.statement: GKE's built-in Artifact Registry pulls use the Pod's Workload Identity Federation for GKE identity.
en.explanation: GKE uses the node pool's configured IAM service account to pull container images, including when Workload Identity Federation for GKE is enabled.

source.title: About Workload Identity Federation for GKE

en.statement: Customers remain responsible for information and data stored in cloud services.
en.explanation: Customers retain responsibility for their cloud data, including its classification, protection, and governance.

en.statement: Azure CLI can run Azure management commands from a shell script on Linux or macOS.
en.explanation: Azure CLI is a cross-platform command-line tool for managing Azure resources and can be used in shell scripts.

en.statement: Azure Monitor platform metrics for a virtual machine require an agent inside the guest OS.
en.explanation: Azure Monitor collects platform metrics automatically from Azure resources. A guest OS agent is needed for guest metrics, not platform metrics.

source.title: Azure Monitor supported metrics and data collection

en.statement: Azure App Service can host web applications and REST APIs on a managed web platform.
en.explanation: Azure App Service handles the hosting platform for web apps and REST APIs, letting developers focus on application code.

en.statement: A diagnostic setting on an Azure resource sends its resource logs to destinations such as a Log Analytics workspace.
en.explanation: Resource logs aren't collected by default. A diagnostic setting picks the log categories to collect and sends them to destinations such as a Log Analytics workspace, a storage account or an event hub.

source.title: Collect resource logs from an Azure resource

en.statement: Azure Monitor Application Insights requires a web app to run on Azure App Service.
en.explanation: Azure Monitor Application Insights can monitor applications hosted on Azure, on-premises, or other clouds; Azure App Service hosting is optional.

en.statement: An Azure blob in the archive tier can be read immediately through its usual endpoint.
en.explanation: Archive blobs are offline and need rehydration to an online tier before they can be read.

en.statement: In PaaS, the provider maintains the operating system and managed runtime.
en.explanation: The PaaS provider manages platform components such as the operating system, middleware, and runtime.

en.statement: Microsoft Entra ID provides managed LDAP and Kerberos services for legacy applications.
en.explanation: Microsoft Entra Domain Services provides managed LDAP and Kerberos for legacy applications; Microsoft Entra ID is the cloud identity service.

source.title: What is Microsoft Entra Domain Services?

en.statement: Cloud autoscaling also scales capacity back in, removing resources once a traffic peak subsides.
en.explanation: Microsoft Learn describes scaling in, like scaling out, as something that happens automatically or manually, so capacity added for a peak can be removed as demand falls.

source.title: Describe the benefits of high availability and scalability in the cloud

en.statement: Azure retains a VM's Standard public IP address when an administrator stops and deallocates the VM.
en.explanation: Standard public IPs use static allocation. Deallocating the VM leaves its public IP resource and assigned address in place.

en.statement: A Reader assignment lets its holder retrieve a storage account's access keys through Azure Resource Manager.
en.explanation: Reader exposes control-plane information but excludes the action that lists storage account keys.

source.title: Choose how to authorize access to blob data in the Azure portal

en.statement: Moving an Azure VM to another resource group changes the resource ID used by management scripts.
en.explanation: A VM's resource ID includes its resource group. After moving the VM, update management references that still contain the old resource ID.

source.title: Move resources to a new resource group or subscription

en.statement: Azure accepts a network interface into an application security group only from the first member's virtual network.
en.explanation: The first network interface added establishes an application security group's virtual network. Subsequent member interfaces belong to that same network.

en.statement: An administrator directly obtains a VM NIC's effective routes by listing its subnet's user-defined routes.
en.explanation: Inspect effective routes on the VM's network interface to see the combined routing information. Listing the subnet's user-defined routes omits other route sources.

source.title: Create, change, or delete a route table

en.statement: For routes with the same matching prefix, Azure chooses a user-defined route ahead of a BGP route.
en.explanation: When matching prefixes are equal, Azure ranks a user-defined route ahead of one learned through BGP. This lets an administrator override that advertised path.

en.statement: Administrators configure Azure Disk Backup in a Recovery Services vault to protect a managed disk.
en.explanation: Configure Azure Disk Backup in a Backup vault. The managed disk's backup instance and policy belong to that vault.

en.statement: Azure Resource Manager masks a secure parameter's value inside an ordinary string deployment output.
en.explanation: An ordinary string output exposes the secure parameter's value in deployment history. The parameter's secure type does not transfer protection to that output.

source.title: Test cases for ARM templates: Outputs cannot include secrets

en.statement: An SMB identity needs both share-level permission and file or directory permission for Azure Files access.
en.explanation: Azure Files checks permissions at the share and at the file or directory. A share-level grant by itself does not grant access to the files inside.

source.title: Overview of Azure Files authorization and access control

en.statement: An alert processing rule that adds action groups overrides a matching rule that suppresses action groups.
en.explanation: A suppression rule takes precedence when addition and suppression rules match the same fired alert. Azure Monitor suppresses the alert's action groups.

source.title: Alert processing rules for Azure Monitor alerts

en.statement: Microsoft Entra Domain Services can extend an on-premises domain with Microsoft-managed domain controllers.
en.explanation: Microsoft Entra Domain Services creates a standalone managed domain. It offers legacy domain protocols for Azure workloads rather than extending the existing on-premises domain.

source.title: What is Microsoft Entra Domain Services?

en.statement: Azure Migrate Collector collects a discovery snapshot in an on-premises network with restricted Azure connectivity.
en.explanation: The Collector scans the estate locally and exports inventory for later upload. Discovery therefore suits environments where continuous Azure connectivity is impractical.

source.title: Discover servers and workloads using Azure Migrate collector

en.statement: In-flight dedicated SQL pool queries keep running while Azure Synapse Analytics scales the pool's compute.
en.explanation: Azure Synapse Analytics cancels dedicated SQL pool queries when scaling is requested and rolls back open transactions before changing compute resources.

source.title: Manage compute in a dedicated SQL pool

en.statement: Azure API Management Premium supports gateways in multiple Azure regions within the same service instance.
en.explanation: Azure API Management Premium deploys regional gateways for geographically distributed callers. Its management plane remains in the primary region.

source.title: Deploy an Azure API Management instance to multiple Azure regions

en.statement: Azure Blob Storage releases a legal hold when the compliance team's retention interval expires.
en.explanation: A legal hold remains in effect until an authorized user explicitly clears it. It suits retention whose end date is unknown.

source.title: Immutable storage for blob data overview

en.statement: A running Azure API Management self-hosted gateway stops serving APIs when its connection to Azure fails.
en.explanation: A running Azure API Management self-hosted gateway continues using its in-memory configuration during a temporary Azure connection loss. Configuration updates and cloud telemetry pause.

en.statement: Azure SQL Database Business Critical supports In-Memory OLTP tables for transaction-heavy applications.
en.explanation: The Business Critical tier includes In-Memory OLTP support, so a design that depends on memory-optimized tables can retain that capability.

source.title: In-memory technologies in Azure SQL Database

en.statement: A managed private endpoint in Azure Data Factory reaches a storage account only after the account's owner approves it.
en.explanation: Creating a managed private endpoint opens a Pending private endpoint connection. The storage account owner approves or rejects it, and only an approved endpoint can send traffic.

source.title: Managed virtual network and managed private endpoints - Azure Data Factory

en.statement: Diagnostic settings support central log routing to a workspace in another subscription with suitable access.
en.explanation: A diagnostic setting may target another subscription when its configuring user has appropriate access to both. This supports centralized logging across subscriptions.

en.statement: Azure App Configuration can copy a secret's value into its store through a Key Vault reference.
en.explanation: Azure App Configuration stores a URI for a Key Vault reference. The application authenticates to Azure Key Vault and retrieves the secret's value.

source.title: Use Key Vault references in an ASP.NET Core app

en.statement: Azure DevOps requires a query in Shared Queries before adding its chart to a dashboard.
en.explanation: Saving the query in a Shared Queries folder makes its chart available to add to a dashboard.

source.title: Configure a chart for work items widget

en.statement: Several self-hosted agent VMs in Azure share one user-assigned managed identity and its role assignments.
en.explanation: A user-assigned managed identity is a standalone Azure resource with its own lifecycle, so agent VMs that are recycled often keep consistent role assignments.

en.statement: Azure Load Testing can execute a k6 script as a pipeline's load test.
en.explanation: Azure Load Testing runs Apache JMeter or Locust scripts; k6 scripts use another test framework.

en.statement: A GitHub user can limit GitHub Actions notifications from watched repositories to failed workflow runs.
en.explanation: The Actions notification setting Only notify for failed workflows delivers workflow run updates when a run fails.

en.statement: CodeQL run outside the container that compiles the code can fail with No source code was seen during the build.
en.explanation: CodeQL has to monitor a compiled language's build, so GitHub says to run it inside the container in which the code is built, both with the CodeQL CLI and with GitHub Actions.

source.title: Running CodeQL code scanning in a container

en.statement: GitHub reserves access to view active repository rulesets for repository administrators.
en.explanation: People with repository read access can inspect active rulesets.

en.statement: An Allow permission on a security group gives a Basic user test case management in Azure Test Plans.
en.explanation: Test case management comes with Basic + Test Plans or an applicable Visual Studio subscription; to give a user such features, change the access level, not permissions.

en.statement: GitHub lets a repository administrator add a specific GitHub App to a ruleset's bypass list.
en.explanation: A ruleset can grant a named GitHub App an exception to its protections.

en.statement: Azure Resource Manager leaves properties omitted from a template unchanged in an incremental redeployment.
en.explanation: Incremental deployment reapplies all of a resource's properties, so properties omitted from the template are reset to their default values; specify every non-default value.

en.statement: Publishers send new Azure Artifacts package versions directly to the @release view.
en.explanation: Publish packages to the base feed, then promote chosen versions to @release.

en.statement: An Azure OpenAI v1 developer sets OpenAI() base_url to the resource endpoint ending in /openai/v1/.
en.explanation: The OpenAI Python client targets Azure OpenAI v1 through base_url, including the /openai/v1/ route.

en.statement: In Foundry Agents v2, a developer who saves edited instructions for an agent creates a new agent version.
en.explanation: Saved Foundry agent versions are immutable, so any change is saved as a new version. Code refers to an agent as <agent_name>:<version>.

source.title: Agent development lifecycle in Microsoft Foundry

en.statement: Foundry prompt-agent tracing can capture tool-call arguments when project tracing is enabled.
en.explanation: Tool arguments can enter Foundry prompt-agent trace telemetry. Developers redact secrets and personal data before those values enter telemetry.

source.title: Set up tracing in Microsoft Foundry

en.statement: Foundry content safety evaluators use the developer's model deployment to score harmful response content.
en.explanation: Foundry content safety evaluators use Microsoft's hosted safety models. Developers supply Foundry project information rather than a judge deployment_name.

en.statement: An Azure AI Search app uses semantic reranking to fetch documents missed by its first retrieval stage.
en.explanation: Semantic ranker reorders documents supplied by initial retrieval. Increase the initial candidate set when relevant documents are missing.

source.title: Semantic ranking in Azure AI Search

en.statement: Azure OpenAI v1 apps use detail=high on input_image to increase the Responses API's output-token limit.
en.explanation: Responses API detail controls image processing fidelity, rather than output-token limits.

source.title: Use the Azure OpenAI Responses API

en.statement: An app using Azure Translator Text API v3.0 omits from to select source-language detection.
en.explanation: Translator Text API v3.0 detects the input language when from is omitted. This suits plain-text requests whose source language the app does not already know.

en.statement: An Azure AI Search vectorizer generates document embeddings during an indexer's ingestion pipeline.
en.explanation: An Azure AI Search vectorizer converts query input to vectors at query time. Indexing uses embedding skills.

source.title: Integrated vector embedding in Azure AI Search

en.statement: Azure OpenAI v1 structured outputs keep nullable properties in the schema's required list.
en.explanation: A nullable property still appears as a key in structured output. Declare it required and include null in its type to represent an optional value.

source.title: How to use structured outputs with Azure OpenAI

en.statement: Content Understanding 2025-11-01 sends an unfamiliar document to an implicit other category.
en.explanation: An app defines an explicit catch-all category for unmatched documents. Otherwise, Content Understanding assigns a category from the app's configured list.

en.statement: Different product ID arguments give a 'use cache' function separate entries.
en.explanation: A cached function's serialized arguments contribute to its cache key, separating results for different product IDs.

en.statement: A Transition replaces revealed content with a fallback when the same Suspense boundary suspends again.
en.explanation: A Transition keeps already revealed content visible when its update suspends, rather than replacing it with a loading fallback.
In the previous model, dynamic = 'force-dynamic' bypasses persistent fetch caching for the route.

en.statement: The Client Cache retains its stored route payloads across a full page reload in the same browser tab.
en.explanation: A full page reload clears the Client Cache; its previously stored route payloads do not survive the reload.

en.statement: A shared layout stays interactive while loading.js displays feedback for the incoming route.
en.explanation: During navigation, loading.js can show a loading view while the shared layout continues responding to interaction.

en.statement: In the Pages Router, fallback: 'blocking' shows a loading fallback while generating a new path.
en.explanation: With fallback: 'blocking', the initial request for a new path waits for generated HTML instead of receiving a loading fallback.

en.statement: One page can combine build-time HTML with request-time personalized content.
en.explanation: Partial Prerendering allows a build-time shell alongside personalized sections completed after a request arrives.

en.statement: Passing dynamic children through a 'use cache' wrapper caches those children.
en.explanation: Children passed through a cached wrapper as an opaque slot can remain dynamic; the wrapper does not cache their rendered content.

en.statement: A cacheLife entry past its expire limit serves stale data during regeneration.
en.explanation: After the expire limit, the next request waits for fresh computation rather than receiving the expired cached value.

en.statement: Date objects are supported props from a Server Component to a Client Component.
en.explanation: React includes Date among the built-in types its server-to-client serialization supports.

en.statement: A Fragment groups sibling JSX elements and renders their DOM nodes directly.
en.explanation: A Fragment provides a JSX parent while adding no wrapper element to the browser's DOM tree.

en.statement: A Server Component can pass a plain local callback as an onClick prop to a Client Component.
en.explanation: Props crossing from a Server Component to a Client Component must be serializable; a plain local callback cannot cross that boundary.

en.statement: Passing createItems() to useState defers that call until state initialization.
en.explanation: JavaScript calls createItems() while evaluating the argument on each render. Passing createItems as an initializer lets React call it during initialization.

en.statement: Calling useState inside an onClick handler follows the Rules of Hooks.
en.explanation: Event handlers run in response to interactions, outside the component's rendering call where Hooks belong.

en.statement: React's documentation recommends grouping state values that change together.
en.explanation: When values change together, grouping them in one state variable helps keep their updates in sync.

en.statement: In React 19, <ThemeContext value={theme}> supplies context to its descendants.
en.explanation: React 19 lets a context object render directly as its provider. <ThemeContext.Provider> remains the legacy provider form.

en.statement: useCallback invokes the supplied function during the render that declares it.
en.explanation: useCallback returns the function value; it does not call that function. The caller decides when to invoke it.

en.statement: A useRef object keeps the same identity across its component's renders.
en.explanation: React returns the same ref object on later renders, so current retains information between them.

en.statement: Two components calling the same custom Hook can share the Hook's local useState state.
en.explanation: Each call to a custom Hook has independent local state. Reusing the Hook's code does not merge its callers' useState values.

en.statement: React generally runs Effects after paint for updates outside user interactions.
en.explanation: For an update unrelated to an interaction, React generally lets the browser paint the updated screen before running the Effect.

en.statement: The Vue Router documentation recommends defineAsyncComponent() for route components that load lazily.
en.explanation: A lazy route component is a plain function that returns a dynamic import; the docs advise against using async components as route components.

en.statement: Vue forwards the values following the event name in an emit() call to the parent listener.
en.explanation: Additional emit() arguments become listener arguments in the same order.

en.statement: In Pinia, an action can be async and await API calls or other actions before it changes state.
en.explanation: Unlike getters, actions can be asynchronous; any library that returns a Promise works, and an action can use other stores.

en.statement: The Vue Router documentation recommends the HTML5 history mode created with createWebHistory().
en.explanation: createWebHistory() produces normal-looking URLs; the server needs a catch-all fallback to index.html so direct visits to deep URLs load the app.

en.statement: Hand-written render functions receive the same compile-time optimizations as Vue templates.
en.explanation: Vue's compiler optimizes templates through static analysis. Hand-written render functions receive fewer compile-time optimizations.

source.title: Rendering Mechanism: Templates vs. Render Functions

en.statement: Vue's documentation recommends keeping mutations of provided reactive state in the provider.
en.explanation: Keeping provided state and its mutations together simplifies maintenance.

en.statement: The browser compiles a Single-File Component's template when the component first mounts.
en.explanation: @vue/compiler-sfc pre-compiles SFCs into standard ES modules as part of the build.

en.statement: In Vue Router, a child route path that starts with / resolves relative to its parent route's path.
en.explanation: Vue Router treats a nested path starting with / as a root path, which keeps the component nesting without a nested URL.

en.statement: On a text input, v-model.lazy synchronizes the bound state after change events.
en.explanation: The .lazy modifier makes text-input v-model listen for change events.

en.statement: `defineProps({ enabled: Boolean })` gives enabled the value false when the parent omits it.
en.explanation: An absent Boolean prop casts to false under this declaration.

en.statement: In Angular v22, Signal Forms supports a Map as a structural model container for nested fields.
en.explanation: Signal Forms builds nested field structure from plain objects and arrays. A Map is not a supported structural container.

en.statement: ng update leaves source-code migrations to the developer after updating Angular package versions.
en.explanation: ng update runs applicable migration schematics, which can transform application code as part of the dependency update.

en.statement: Since Angular v22, Angular marks the webpack builders in @angular-devkit/build-angular as deprecated.
en.explanation: Angular v22 marks @angular-devkit/build-angular's webpack builders as deprecated and directs projects toward @angular/build.

en.statement: ViewEncapsulation.Emulated isolates component elements from matching global style rules.
en.explanation: Global styles can still affect elements inside a component using Emulated encapsulation.

en.statement: With SSR, Angular creates a fresh value for a top-level useValue provider for each request.
en.explanation: Top-level useValue values persist across server requests. Angular establishes those values when the application code is first evaluated.

en.statement: An effect created in a root-provided service's constructor outlives the component that injected the service.
en.explanation: Effects created while a root-provided service is instantiated are root effects: Angular destroys them with the application, or when code calls destroy() on the returned EffectRef.

en.statement: Angular executes afterNextRender callbacks during server rendering after producing the page's HTML.
en.explanation: afterNextRender callbacks execute in the browser; Angular skips them during server rendering and build-time prerendering.

en.statement: Angular template expressions support arrow functions that use an expression body.
en.explanation: Template arrow functions use an expression after =>; block-bodied arrow functions are rejected.

en.statement: Angular automatically ends programmatic subscriptions to an output() when its owning component is destroyed.
en.explanation: An output() returns an OutputEmitterRef. Angular drops the listeners registered with its subscribe() when the owning directive or component is destroyed, so no manual unsubscribe is needed.

en.statement: A linkedSignal computation with an explicit source can inspect its previous linked value.
en.explanation: The optional previous object exposes previous.value, letting the computation preserve earlier linked state.

en.statement: Browser mount skips initial intro transitions by default.
en.explanation: Initial mount transitions play unless intro is false.

en.statement: Svelte passes the DOM element to the function used in {@attach setup}.
en.explanation: An attachment's element argument gives setup access to that mounted node.

en.statement: Svelte's docs recommend bind:group rather than bind:checked for radio inputs.
en.explanation: Radio inputs bound to the same variable with bind:group are mutually exclusive, and that variable holds the value of the selected radio.

en.statement: A provider's local $state reassignment automatically replaces the object held by existing context consumers.
en.explanation: Context consumers retain the object originally provided. Reassigning the provider's local variable leaves that reference intact.

en.statement: <svelte:body> supports a use: action applied to the browser's document.body element.
en.explanation: The body helper accepts use: directives for integrating behavior with document.body.

en.statement: A $state.raw array can hold separately reactive $state objects.
en.explanation: Reactive $state members retain reactivity inside $state.raw containers.

en.statement: Svelte renders an {#each} block's {:else} branch for an empty array.
en.explanation: An {#each} else branch supplies empty-list content.

en.statement: An unchanged primitive $derived result still triggers its dependent DOM text update.
en.explanation: Svelte skips updates for referentially identical results.

en.statement: Developers directly increment a $state number to update its displayed value.

en.explanation: The later color attribute wins over the preceding spread.

en.statement: A `var` declared inside an `if` block belongs to the surrounding function's scope.
en.explanation: Within a function, an if block does not introduce a scope for var. Code elsewhere in that function can access the same binding.

en.statement: For `function C(){}`, `new (C.bind({}))()` gives `C` a fresh object as `this`.
en.explanation: Constructing a bound function uses a fresh receiver for its target constructor. The receiver supplied to bind is ignored.

en.statement: Since ES2023, `[20, 3].toSorted()` returns the array `[3, 20]` with its default comparison.
en.explanation: toSorted uses string comparison by default, so '20' precedes '3'. Sorting [20, 3] with that default produces [20, 3].

en.statement: Calling a promise's `reject` function after it fulfills changes the promise to rejected.
en.explanation: A fulfilled promise stays fulfilled. Later calls to its reject callback have no effect on the promise's state or fulfillment value.

en.statement: Since ES2023, `toSorted()`, `toReversed()`, `toSpliced()`, and `with()` mutate their source array.
en.explanation: These copying array methods return new arrays, preserving the source array. Their edits affect the returned array rather than the original.

en.statement: Updating an existing Map entry with `set()` preserves that key's position in iteration order.
en.explanation: Map iteration follows the order in which keys were first inserted. Setting a new value for a key already present keeps its original position.

en.statement: Since ES2024, `Promise.withResolvers()` returns a promise with attached `resolve` and `reject` methods.
en.explanation: Promise.withResolvers() returns an object with promise, resolve, and reject properties. The functions sit alongside the promise property rather than being attached to the promise.

en.statement: Calling a generator function executes its body through the first `yield` before returning.
en.explanation: Calling a generator function creates a generator object and leaves its body suspended. Its first next() call starts executing the body.

en.statement: Since ES2025, `Promise.try(fn)` invokes `fn` synchronously during the call.
en.explanation: Promise.try invokes its callback before returning to its caller. The callback's initial side effects therefore happen during that call.

en.statement: `Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER` is the largest representable integer of the Number type.
en.explanation: Number represents some integers above Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER exactly, but loses the ability to distinguish consecutive integers reliably beyond the safe range.

en.statement: With `noImplicitAny` disabled, an uninferred parameter gets type `unknown`.
en.explanation: An unannotated parameter with no inferred type falls back to `any`. Disabling `noImplicitAny` suppresses the error about that fallback.

en.statement: When two `interface Doc` declarations merge, TypeScript tries the earlier declaration's overloads first in a call.
en.explanation: For a merged interface, overload resolution tries the later declaration's overload group first, each group in its own order. Signatures with a single string literal parameter type go before the rest.

en.statement: In `enum E { A = "a" }`, `E["a"]` yields the member name `"A"`.
en.explanation: String enum members get no reverse mapping. The generated enum object has no `"a"` key mapped to `"A"`.

en.statement: In `enum E { A = "a", B = A }`, TypeScript assigns `E.B` the string value `"a"`.
en.explanation: A string enum member can initialize from another string enum member, so `B` receives `A`'s value, `"a"`.

en.statement: With `isolatedModules`, code can reference ambient `const enum` members.
en.explanation: An ambient `const enum` has no emitted value, and `isolatedModules` rejects member references because single-file transpilation cannot inline them.

en.statement: `{ id: string } & { active: boolean }` accepts an object with just `id`.
en.explanation: The intersection combines both object requirements. A value also needs the `active` property.

en.statement: `[K in keyof T]+?` makes existing required properties optional.
en.explanation: The `+?` mapping modifier adds optionality to generated properties. TypeScript also treats an unprefixed `?` as `+?`.

en.statement: Unrelated classes with identically named private members are assignment-compatible.
en.explanation: For a private member in the target, the corresponding source member must originate from the same class declaration. Matching names in unrelated classes do not suffice.

en.statement: `let mode = 'open'` infers `mode` as `string` rather than the literal type.
en.explanation: A `let` binding can later receive another string, so TypeScript widens the initializer's string literal type to `string`.

en.statement: In `enum E { A = 4, B }`, TypeScript assigns `E.B` the numeric value `5`.
en.explanation: A numeric enum member after a constant numeric member auto-increments the preceding value, so `B` is `5`.

en.statement: `revert-layer` restores an earlier declaration for the property in its current cascade layer.
en.explanation: The revert-layer keyword removes its layer's contribution for the property and exposes lower-priority layers or the previous origin.

source.title: CSS Cascading and Inheritance Level 5: revert-layer

en.statement: When `min-width` exceeds `max-width`, the minimum width wins.
en.explanation: A conflicting maximum width does not force the used width below the specified minimum width.

en.statement: In `animation: fade 2s 1s`, the browser assigns the first time value to the delay.
en.explanation: In animation: fade 2s 1s, the first time value sets animation-duration to 2s. The second sets animation-delay to 1s.

en.statement: A child's `box-sizing` follows its parent's computed value through CSS inheritance.
en.explanation: Box-sizing is a non-inherited property. A child's value comes from its own declarations or defaulting.

en.statement: `repeat(auto-fill, 1fr)` creates as many equal fractional columns as fit in a grid container.
en.explanation: auto-fill requires a fixed-size track definition; bare 1fr does not qualify. A bounded form such as minmax(100px, 1fr) qualifies.

en.statement: A relatively positioned block keeps its original layout space when an inset shifts its visible position.
en.explanation: Relative positioning offsets a box after normal layout. Surrounding boxes keep the space allocated for its original position.

en.statement: `all: initial` resets an element's unregistered custom properties to their initial values.
en.explanation: The all shorthand leaves custom properties unchanged. It also excludes direction and unicode-bidi.

en.statement: `z-index` controls the stacking of flex and grid items whose `position` is `static`.
en.explanation: Flex and grid items use z-index for their stack level even while statically positioned. Their item status makes z-index applicable.

en.statement: `article > p` matches a paragraph whose immediate parent is an article.
en.explanation: The > relationship connects a paragraph to its immediate article parent. An intervening ancestor places the paragraph outside this selector's match.

en.statement: For an undeclared `--gap` registered as `<length>` with an initial-value, `var(--gap, 1rem)` returns that initial-value.
en.explanation: A registered property with a non-universal syntax and an initial-value substitutes that initial value when no other declaration applies, so var() leaves the 1rem fallback unused.

en.statement: Tailwind inserts @utility definitions into its components layer alongside component styles.
en.explanation: Tailwind inserts custom utilities into the utilities layer.

en.statement: Tailwind replaces an unresolved --value() declaration with the property's initial value.
en.explanation: Tailwind omits declarations whose --value() calls fail to resolve.

en.statement: Tailwind's sm: utilities target viewports below the sm threshold.
en.explanation: Tailwind generates a minimum-width condition for sm:.

en.statement: Tailwind's in-focus: variant reacts to focus on any parent element, whether or not that parent has the group class.
en.explanation: The in-* variants respond to a state change in any ancestor and need no marker class, so in-focus: also fires when an outer wrapper higher up receives focus.

en.statement: Tailwind resolves @source paths relative to the build's working directory.
en.explanation: Tailwind resolves @source paths from the stylesheet.

en.statement: Tailwind excludes the md boundary from max-md: rules.
en.explanation: Tailwind's max-md: uses a strict upper comparison.

en.statement: For equally specific, equally important active utilities, later class-attribute order decides the winner.
en.explanation: For comparable utilities, Tailwind's stylesheet rule order resolves conflicts.

en.statement: In Tailwind CSS v4, a normal utility beats a conflicting normal @layer components rule with a more specific selector.
en.explanation: Tailwind orders its utilities layer after components; for declarations without !important a later cascade layer wins whatever the selector specificity.

en.statement: With @theme { --tab-size-team: 8; }, @utility tab-* { tab-size: --value(--tab-size-*); } gives tab-team tab-size: 8.
en.explanation: Tailwind resolves the team suffix against --tab-size-team.

en.statement: Tailwind's data-active: waits for data-active to equal 'true'.
A browser separates Web Storage and IndexedDB data by origin.
en.explanation: Web Storage and IndexedDB allocate data by origin, so a script from one origin cannot access another origin's store.

en.statement: X-Frame-Options: SAMEORIGIN checks just the immediate parent in nested frames.
en.explanation: SAMEORIGIN requires every ancestor frame to share the protected page's origin, not merely its immediate parent.

en.statement: For cross-origin SRI, a matching hash replaces the need for Access-Control-Allow-Origin.
en.explanation: A cross-origin SRI load also needs the resource server to pass the CORS check, using an appropriate Access-Control-Allow-Origin response header.

en.statement: A failed CORS check can tell page JavaScript which response header caused the failure.
en.explanation: JavaScript receives a generic CORS failure. The browser console provides the specific reason for debugging.

en.statement: report-to selects a named CSP endpoint defined by Reporting-Endpoints.
en.explanation: The Reporting-Endpoints response header defines a named URL, and the CSP report-to directive selects that name for violation reports.

en.statement: A script-created about:blank popup gets an opaque origin separate from its creator.
en.explanation: A script-created about:blank document inherits the origin of the document that created it.

en.statement: DOM-based XSS requires a changed server HTML response after the attacker supplies input.
en.explanation: With DOM-based XSS, unsafe client code reacts to changes in the browser's DOM environment; the server's HTML response can remain unchanged.

en.statement: In the OWASP Top 10:2025, A08:2025 Software or Data Integrity Failures uses signatures to verify updates.
en.explanation: A08 recommends digital signatures or similar checks to confirm an update's expected source and detect modification.

source.title: A08 Software or Data Integrity Failures - OWASP Top 10:2025

en.statement: In the OWASP Top 10:2025, A02:2025 Security Misconfiguration describes servers returning stack traces to users.
en.explanation: A02 counts error handling that returns stack traces or other overly informative messages to users as misconfiguration, and advises central interception of such messages.

en.statement: A clickjacking page puts a transparent target iframe over a decoy button.
en.explanation: The victim sees the decoy but clicks a sensitive control in the transparent target page layered over it.

en.statement: In the APG menu pattern, Escape returns focus from an open submenu to the item that opened it.
en.explanation: The APG uses Escape to dismiss the menu containing focus and restore focus to its launching context. For a submenu, that context is its parent menu item.

source.title: Menu and Menubar Pattern - ARIA Authoring Practices Guide

en.statement: A `<header>` inside an `<article>` supplies the document's implicit banner landmark.
en.explanation: A header nested inside article content does not receive the implicit banner role. The banner mapping is for the page-level header, subject to the nesting restrictions.

source.title: ARIA: banner role - MDN Web Docs

en.statement: The WAI tutorial recommends "Printer icon" as the alternative for an image that serves as a Print button.
en.explanation: A functional image's alternative identifies its action or destination, such as "Print". Describing the object alone misses the control's purpose.

en.statement: WCAG permits authors to exclude an inaccessible sidebar when evaluating the rest of a page for conformance.
en.explanation: Conformance applies to a complete page. Authors cannot declare a selected region conformant while excluding an inaccessible sidebar.

en.statement: Non-text Contrast (Level AA) sets 3:1 for an active checkbox's state mark when authors style that mark.
en.explanation: Non-text Contrast (Level AA) evaluates the mark needed to recognize a checkbox state against adjacent colors. The requirement concerns visual identification, not decorative parts.

en.statement: Browsers give `<div role="button">` Enter-key activation through its ARIA role.
en.explanation: role="button" supplies semantics, not keyboard activation. Authors implement the key handling for a custom div button.

source.title: ARIA: button role - MDN Web Docs

en.statement: Contrast (Minimum) (Level AA) uses unrounded computed ratios when authors assess text contrast.
en.explanation: Threshold comparisons use the computed ratio's full precision. Rounding a result for display does not make a below-threshold contrast ratio pass.

en.statement: No Keyboard Trap (Level A) calls for instructions when a component uses a nonstandard keyboard exit.
en.explanation: No Keyboard Trap (Level A) allows a nonstandard keyboard escape method if users receive instructions. The instructions explain how to move focus out of the component.

en.statement: Contrast (Minimum) (Level AA) sets a 4.5:1 floor for paragraph text outside its exceptions.
en.explanation: Contrast (Minimum) (Level AA) compares text with its background. Meeting the threshold helps users with reduced contrast sensitivity read the text.

en.statement: In WAI-ARIA 1.2, the `status` role gives its updates the implicit `aria-live="assertive"` priority.
en.explanation: WAI-ARIA 1.2 gives status an implicit aria-live="polite" value. Its default priority suits advisory updates rather than urgent interruptions.

source.title: ARIA: status role - MDN Web Docs

en.statement: font-display: optional can replace visible fallback text with a web font that arrives late.
en.explanation: The optional strategy has no swap period. A font that misses its brief block period leaves the fallback in use for that visit.

en.statement: A LayoutShift entry's sources list identifies the element responsible for causing the movement.
en.explanation: LayoutShift.sources lists elements that moved; their movement may instead originate from another element being inserted or resized.

en.statement: An element with display: none keeps a layout box in the browser's render tree.
en.explanation: display: none excludes the element and its descendants from the render tree, so they occupy no layout space.

en.statement: WOFF2 uses Brotli compression to reduce the amount of font data a browser downloads.
en.explanation: Brotli compression helps WOFF2 deliver font data in smaller files than WOFF, reducing transfer work.

en.statement: Chrome exposes cross-origin iframe blocking details through its notRestoredReasons API.
en.explanation: For cross-origin frames, Chrome masks the detailed reasons; the top-level report can include a masked reason instead.

en.statement: In Chrome, a page served with Cache-Control: no-store can qualify for the bfcache.
en.explanation: Chrome permits no-store pages under extra restrictions and evicts them when cookies or other authorization methods change.

en.statement: The browser derives an image's initial aspect ratio from its HTML width and height attributes.
en.explanation: Image width and height attributes supply an initial aspect ratio, allowing the browser to reserve space before image loading finishes.

en.statement: web.dev measures LCP resource load delay from TTFB until the LCP resource request starts.
en.explanation: Resource load delay captures the gap before the browser begins fetching the LCP resource.

en.statement: web.dev accepts two good Core Web Vitals out of three as a pass.
en.explanation: web.dev says tools should award a pass when all three Core Web Vitals meet their good targets.

en.statement: The HTML Standard requires modulepreload to fetch the target module's dependencies.
en.explanation: The HTML Standard makes fetching dependencies an optional optimization when the browser processes modulepreload.

en.statement: An HTTP/1.1 proxy removes fields named by Connection before forwarding an HTTP message.
en.explanation: A forwarding proxy removes fields nominated by Connection because those fields apply to the incoming connection.
